key_insight: Dream to Remember (D2R) continually adapts a frozen generalist robot policy to new tasks by using a pretrained world model to rehearse old skills, reducing catastrophic forgetting without replay data.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical continual-learning recipe for robotics: improve sequential task performance while preserving prior capabilities using fixed policy backbones and imagined rollouts.
method: Keep the base generalist policy frozen and train only a steering module.
Use a frozen world model to generate imagined rollouts that anchor earlier behaviors during new-task learning.
If the world model is accurate enough, train fully in imagination; otherwise learn new tasks in the environment while still rehearsing old tasks in imagination.
evidence_signal: On CALVIN, D2R raised average success from 63.7% to 74.8% across eight sequential tasks in imagination, while LoRA fine-tuning fell to 11.7%; it also retained performance on LIBERO and improved three real-robot Franka tasks.
watch_item: The approach depends on the fidelity of the pretrained world model; when it is not accurate enough, it may only support rehearsal of prior tasks rather than safe or effective optimization of new ones.
paper_title: Dream to Remember: Continual Steering of Generalist Robot Policies with World Models
